title: Creating Ethics-based Education System Centred on Character and Not Grades
what_it_is: Creating Ethics-based Education System Centred on Character and Not Grades

sections.label: Six key values framework
sections.summary: A framework of six key values shapes the curriculum, and schools dedicate one to two hours weekly to character and citizenship teaching.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: To guide our work in this area, we have a framework of six key values that shape our curriculum and these six key values are Respect, Responsibility, Resilience, Integrity, Care and Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: In order to set the foundations of character development and sound values, schools dedicate generally between one and two hours per week to teach character and citizenship as well as social and emotional competencies.

sections.label: Students cleaning school environment
sections.summary: Acting Minister Ng Chee Meng announced letting students participate in daily cleaning of their school environment.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Acting Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Acting Minister for Education (Schools))
sentences.text: The latest move last week announced by Acting Minister Ng Chee Meng to let our students participate in the daily cleaning of their school environment is one good example.

sections.label: Broad-based approach in sports
sections.summary: Schools have focused on a broad-based approach giving students opportunities to experience various sports without prior foundation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: In the area of sports, our schools have also, in the last few years, focused on a broad-based approach: giving our students an opportunity to experience various types of sports even if they did not have a foundation in the particular sports.

sections.label: CCE hours at pre-University
sections.summary: Generally 80 hours are allocated for CCE lessons at pre-University levels across two to three years, split equally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Generally, 80 hours are allocated for CCE lessons at the pre-University levels across two to three years of which 40 hours are for CCE lessons and 40 hours are for school-designed CCE.

sections.label: Secondary level CCE hours
sections.summary: At Secondary level, 60 hours per year are allocated to be carried out over two hours per week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the Secondary level, I want to assure the Member that 60 hours per year are allocated to be carried out over two hours per week.

sections.label: Upper Primary CCE hours
sections.summary: At upper Primary level, 60 to 75 hours per year are allocated, including one to two hours weekly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: For the upper Primary level, it would be 60 hours to 75 hours per year, and this includes one to two hours on a weekly basis.

sections.label: Edusave Character Award introduction
sections.summary: MOE introduced the Edusave Character Award in 2012 to let schools recognise students showing exemplary character and outstanding personal qualities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: MOE introduced the Edusave Character Award (ECHA) in 2012, four years ago, to enable our schools to recognise the students who demonstrate exemplary character and outstanding personal qualities through their behaviour and actions.
